temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar year the projection describes, from the provider's Time column. The grain is one row per period, location_id and scenario_id. Every row is a projection, so this table has no estimated period and cannot be read as a continuation of an observed series on its own: the estimates live in the sibling indicator table, and the first year here is the year after the estimates end. Stocks are projected for 1 July and flows are totals over the calendar year. The panel is not rectangular across scenarios: seventeen scenarios cover the world total and every country or area, while the probabilistic 'Mean' is published for countries and areas only and carries the total fertility rate alone. The provider's own 1 January row for the year after the projection horizon is excluded, because it carries a population stock and none of this table's measures. The probabilistic summaries behave differently from the deterministic paths at their edges: a lower bound rounds a small country's population to zero at the far end of the projection and reports a median age no human population could have where it does, and on four rows it publishes a median age of exactly zero beside an ordinary population, which is a placeholder rather than an age. That is the published tail of a distribution rather than a defect, which is why scenario_kind exists and why physical ranges are asserted only of the deterministic scenarios. A consumer reading a median age from a probabilistic bound has to treat zero as no value.

validations.description: There is exactly one observation for each location, calendar year and scenario.
validations.name: one-row-per-location-year-and-scenario

validations.description: Period, location identity and scenario identity are never null, however sparse the measures are.
validations.name: required-identity-is-never-null

validations.description: Each scenario name has exactly one provider code, each code exactly one name, and each scenario exactly one kind.
validations.name: scenario-identity-is-one-to-one

validations.description: Every country or area carries an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, and only the world total does not.
validations.name: only-the-world-total-lacks-an-iso3-code

validations.description: No scenario stops short of or reaches beyond the projection period the others cover.
validations.name: every-scenario-covers-the-same-years

validations.description: Where a scenario publishes a measure it publishes it for every row it covers, so a null marks a measure the scenario does not carry rather than a gap inside one it does.
validations.name: a-scenario-publishes-a-measure-throughout-or-not-at-all

validations.description: No row falls in the estimated period, which belongs to the sibling indicator table rather than to this one.
validations.name: every-year-is-projected

validations.description: Under the deterministic scenarios, projected populations are positive and fertility rates, life expectancies and median ages lie in ranges a human population can take. The probabilistic summaries are held only to non-negativity, because the edges of a distribution are not themselves populations.
validations.name: measures-lie-in-their-published-ranges
